newsitem.title: GERMANY: Frankfurt rules out stake in Cologne airport.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt rules out stake in Cologne airport.

text.p: Frankfurt airport is no longer interested in taking a stake in Cologne/Bonn airport, Flughafen Frankfurt Main AG (FAG) said.

FAG, which owns and manages Frankfurt airport, said its chairman Wilhelm Bender and Lothar Ruschmeier, supervisory board chairman of the Cologne airport authority, held talks on March 25 about areas of co-operation.
The talks, which will be continued, covered all feasible forms of co-operation between the two German airports, an FAG statement said.
"The question of a possible ownership holding (in Cologne airport) was laid aside," it added.

On March 14, Cologne airport played down reports of a possible FAG holding, saying that none of its owners, the German government, the state of North Rhine Westphalia or the city of Cologne, were planning to sell their stakes.
One month earlier, FAG had said that forthcoming co-operation talks with Cologne airport could include FAG buying into the authority. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017
